slot.brief: Wheatstone bridge with one unknown resistance; use balance condition to find it, or find equivalent resistance of unbalanced bridge

stem: In a Wheatstone bridge network, the four arms $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ have resistances $P$, $Q$, $S$, and $R$, respectively. A galvanometer is connected between $B$ and $D$, and a battery across $A$ and $C$. When an unknown resistor of resistance $X$ is connected in parallel with arm $CD$, the bridge balances. If $X$ is instead disconnected from $CD$ and connected in series with arm $DA$, the bridge is again balanced. The value of $X$ must be

verdicts.working: Balance requires P/Q = R_arm/S_arm. With X parallel to CD (S): P/Q = R(S+X)/(SX). With X in series with DA (R): P/Q = (R+X)/S. Equating: R(S+X)/X = R+X ⇒ RS = X² ⇒ X = √(RS). Numeric check (R=3, S=12, X=6) gives both ratios 0.75.

working:
The Wheatstone bridge has arms $AB = P$, $BC = Q$, $DA = R$, and $CD = S$.

In the first case, when resistor $X$ is connected in parallel with arm $CD$, the effective resistance of arm $CD$ becomes:
$$S' = \dfrac{S X}{S + X}$$
The balance condition gives:
$$\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{R}{S'} = \dfrac{R(S + X)}{S X} \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

In the second case, when $X$ is connected in series with arm $DA$, the effective resistance of arm $DA$ becomes:
$$R' = R + X$$
while arm $CD$ has its original resistance $S$. The bridge is again balanced, so:
$$\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{R'}{S} = \dfrac{R + X}{S} \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Equating (1) and (2):
$$\dfrac{R(S + X)}{S X} = \dfrac{R + X}{S}$$

Multiplying both sides by $S$:
$$\dfrac{R(S + X)}{X} = R + X$$
$$\dfrac{RS}{X} + R = R + X$$
$$\dfrac{RS}{X} = X \implies X^2 = RS \implies X = \sqrt{RS}$$

Independent check: Balance requires P/Q = R_arm/S_arm. With X parallel to CD (S): P/Q = R(S+X)/(SX). With X in series with DA (R): P/Q = (R+X)/S. Equating: R(S+X)/X = R+X ⇒ RS = X² ⇒ X = √(RS). Numeric check (R=3, S=12, X=6) gives both ratios 0.75.

C encodes assuming the arithmetic mean of the two arm resistances.
